messages:
devon: Heads-up — saw p99 latency spikes on prod dedicated yesterday ~03:22 UTC, coincident with heavy long-context requests (~25k tokens). :eyes:

maria: Any stack traces or perf dumps?

devon: Quick summary from the perf dump:
```
kv_page_faults=548
eviction_policy=FIFO
kv_frag_ratio=0.73
p50=22ms p95=90ms p99=420ms
hot_threads: memmove, kv_bucket_mutex contended
```
Repro command I used on staging: `./loadtest --model r-infer-2 --seq 25000 --clients 40 --duration 5m`

ashok: Can you try flipping the env to LRU? `REDWOOD_KV_EVICTION=LRU` and same load. Curious if tail drops.

devon: Did that. Tail improved (~p99 -> 180ms) but we still see intermittent ~250ms spikes. Also fragmentation metric falls slower under LRU but eviction churn goes up.

hao: My suspicion: concurrent eviction + reader racing can give incorrect block offsets when a page is reused too soon. We saw one trace where attention looked up a block that had been recycled and the values were from a different sequence id. Not data corruption per se, but wrong KV mapping -> longer decode paths.

perf-bot: Automated flame summary attached: `cpu: 38% memmove, 22% copy_kv_block, 15% kv_bucket_mutex` — lock hold times jump during the fault bursts.

maria: Do we have a minimal repro that hits the race? If yes, we can add an assertion for seq_id mismatch. Otherwise suggest canary a config change.

devon: I have a core + pcap from the offending host: https://artifacts.internal/runtimes/1825/kv-core-03.tar.gz — contains heap snapshot and the trace where attention returned values for a different request id.

ashok: Quick mitigation option: increase eviction hysteresis and backoff aggressive page reuse (`kv_evict_hysteresis_ms += 50`). Also reduce max evict batch size from 128 -> 64 to smooth out lock contention. Both are quick toggles for a canary.

devon: Canary script I ran (staging small pool):
```
export REDWOOD_KV_EVICTION=LRU
export KV_EVICT_MAX_BATCH=64
export KV_EVICT_HYST_MS=120
./canary-deploy --tag=kv-hysteresis-2026-03-17 --route=2% --duration=30m
```
Results: p99 fell to ~150ms for the canary, no correctness assertions fired in 30m run.

hao: Long-term fix: add seq_id + version check in the attention lookup and make block reuse atomic with a compare-exchange on header. That will kill a lot of subtle races. Also add per-bucket eviction stats to measure fragmentation over time.

maria: Agree. Short-term: deploy as ashok suggested to 5% canary, monitor `kv_seq_mismatch` metric and tail latencies. If mismatch >0, rollback.

canary-bot: Canary deployed `kv-hysteresis-2026-03-17` to 5% at 2026-03-17T04:12:00Z. Health checks: ok.

devon: I'll file the follow-up RFC for seq_id atomicity and add tests that intentionally race eviction+read. Assigning tasks below. :thumbsup:

maria: Tasks:
- devon: upload reproducer + cores (done)
- hao: prototype seq_id compare-exchange, add unit test
- ashok: run extended 2h canary with hysteresis toggles and collect per-bucket stats
- eng-sre: watch for `kv_seq_mismatch` and p99 > 200ms, be ready to rollback

ashok: noted, will start the 2h canary at 04:45 UTC.

devon: thanks, team—keeping this thread for traces + quick updates.
